keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 793-799, 5,754 km2. Two enclaves: Ladoga (59.9N 31.5E) and the Mecklenburg coast (54.2N 12.4E). The Viking Age starts with 'the earliest recorded raids by Norsemen in 793'. Staraya Ladoga (opened): 'A Scandinavian settlement was founded in the mid-8th century' and 'Around the 830s or 840s, it was captured by a group of Varangians', so the Ladoga half has a page behind it; the Mecklenburg half is on no page (unverified: page budget). The Vikings page has no infobox area, so no area check is possible.

Cliopatria 800-805, 13,816 km2. Adds Shetland, the Faroes and a Rostov-Yaroslavl enclave. 'Viking influence in the area commenced in the late 8th century' (Scandinavian Scotland); 'Norsemen settled the Faroe Islands in the 9th or 10th century' (History of the Faroe Islands), so the Faroes are probably early; Rostov is on no page opened (the Staraya Ladoga page does not name it). Stands.

Cliopatria 806-813, 14,029 km2. No change from 800. The Danish king Gudfred 'destroyed the Obotrite city of Reric on the southern Baltic coast in 808'; the eight Mecklenburg cells last until 946, exactly the span of the Obotrites row, so they may be Obotrite land, not a Norse settlement. Unverified: page budget.
Cliopatria 814-824, 14,900 km2. Adds a four-cell enclave on Rügen. Page silent. Unverified: page budget.

Cliopatria 825-839, 25,322 km2. Adds Orkney, the Outer Hebrides and the Peene mouth; Rostov grows. Scandinavian presence in Scotland 'increased in the 830s' (the page marks this as needing a citation), a decade after the shape. Stands within the era's precision.

Cliopatria 840-849, 45,155 km2. Adds Caithness and Sutherland (they 'fell under Norse control at an early date'), Argyll, Islay, Mull, Skye, Man and Wolin. 'The Frankish Annales Bertiniani may record the conquest of the Inner Hebrides by Vikings in 847': the Hebridean cells are right from 847 and seven years early in 840-846, so the corrected shape leaves them out for 840-846 and viking-settlements_847 restores the shape for 847-849. The page says Man 'may also have been taken by the Norse in 877' and was 'certainly held by them by 900', so Man's two cells are probably 30 years early (flagged, not changed). [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: from/to (840, 846) set as the entry's own text says (fx-48 handoff), so it no longer overlaps the next keyframe]

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 850-859, 69,895 km2. Adds Frisia, the Garonne mouth, Bayonne, Dublin, Limerick and Truso. Supported (paraphrase): c. 850 Lothair I acknowledged Rorik as ruler of most of Friesland; Vikings settled at the mouth of the Garonne in the 840s; Dublin 'Established: 853' (Kingdom of Dublin). Disagreement: Limerick and Waterford (860) are said to be founded in 'the next eight years' after 914, 60 years after the shape; longphorts 'From 840' may explain a camp. Stands, flagged.
Cliopatria 860-865, 71,734 km2. The Garonne and Bayonne drop out; Novgorod and Waterford appear. Rurik was 'invited to reign in Novgorod in the year 862', two years after the shape; stands.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 866-869, 83,256 km2. Adds a 35-cell Lincolnshire cluster and Beloozero. The Danelaw page dates the army's landing to 865 ('landed a large army in East Anglia') and 'In 867 they captured Northumbria and its capital, York'; Cliopatria adds York only in 870. Shape right for 866; from 867 use the new keyframe viking-settlements_867. The Lincolnshire cluster itself is dated by no page. Great Heathen Army (opened): the first dated stay in Lincolnshire is the winter quarters 'for 872-873 at Torksey in the Kingdom of Lindsey'.

Cliopatria 870-874, 120,108 km2. Adds Yorkshire (89 cells), East Anglia (46) and south-west Iceland (17). 'the Danes continued their invasion in 869 by defeating King Edmund of East Anglia at Hoxne'; 'Iceland was first settled around 870' (Viking expansion). Stands.

Cliopatria 875-875, 133,516 km2. Iceland grows to 72 cells; Mercia and Cambridge are added ('the Danes ... attacked Mercia, a campaign that lasted until 874'); Wareham appears; Caithness and the Northern Isles leave because Harald 'incorporated the Northern Isles into his kingdom in 875'. Stands.

Cliopatria 876-877, 134,483 km2. Adds Exeter (3 cells). Danelaw timeline: '876: The Danes broke the peace when they captured the fortress of Wareham, followed by a similar capture of Exeter in 877' (the body text says 876 for both). The Exeter cells are corrected to 877; the rest of the shape stands, including one more cell in East Frisia (53.1N 7.6E) that appears in 876 on no page. In 876 Halfdan shared out Northumbrian land, founding the Danelaw (Viking expansion, paraphrase).

Cliopatria 886-891, 50,375 km2. Frisia leaves (paraphrase: Godfrid was assassinated in 885, ending Viking rule of Frisia); a 15-cell Seine-Oise cluster appears. Siege of Paris (opened): '25 November 885 - October 886', Rollo 'stayed behind with his men' after Sigfred left in April 886, and the Vikings 'withdrew from France the next spring' (887); the page has nothing on the Seine or the Oise after 887, so the cluster's last four years are Cliopatria's. Stands.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 892-910, 48,356 km2. Adds a seven-cell Kent cluster; the Seine cluster leaves. Dublin: Ivarr II was 'Driven from Dublin in 902 by native Irish' and 'Dublin abandoned by the Norse from 902 to 917' (Kingdom of Dublin), but the shape keeps Dublin. Use _897 for 897-901 (no Kent) and _902 for 902-910 (no Kent, no Dublin). keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 911-921, 55,666 km2. Normandy (36 cells around Rouen) replaces Kent: 'In 911 Rollo entered vassalage to Charles the Simple' through the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte and became 'the first Norman Count of Rouen' (Viking expansion). A vassal count of the West Franks is not Viking territory: the Duchy of Normandy dossier founds the duchy in 911 on this land (its ledger 0, from the West Franks), so the cells are removed here. Dublin was abandoned 902-917 (Kingdom of Dublin), so for 911-916 use viking-settlements_911b (Normandy and Dublin removed).

Cliopatria 922-925, 86,450 km2. Normandy (36 cells) leaves for the Duchy of Normandy row (already removed from 911 here); Brittany and the Cotentin (139 cells) and Cork (4) appear. Alan II 'expelled the Vikings/Norsemen from Brittany after an occupation that lasted from 907 to about 939': the page makes it an occupation of the Kingdom of Brittany, not Viking territory, and the Cotentin went to Normandy in 933 (Normandy and Brittany dossiers). The 139 cells are removed; the ledger's occupation events (907-939) carry the hatched land.

Cliopatria 947-979, 28,328 km2. Brittany (already removed here for 922-946), Mecklenburg and the Peene mouth leave; a five-cell Oder-mouth cluster appears. Jomsborg 'existed between the 960s and 1043' and 'was built by the Danish king Harold Bluetooth ... in the 960s' (Jomsborg), so the cluster may be Jomsborg and then starts 15 years early and lasts longer than the shape (to 979 here, gone from 980). Cliopatria 980-999, 25,104 km2. Wolin and Limerick leave (one more cell appears near Limerick, 52.7N 8.4W, on no page). Right for 980-999: Greenland is not in this shape, and it does not belong in it: the Norse Greenland dossier founds the colony in 986 and carries it from then. The Hebrides, Skye, Argyll and Man (27 cells) stay in the shape: Scandinavian Scotland has the Hebrides under Scandinavian rulers from 'at least the late tenth century' and Norwegian overlordship only 'by 1098', so nothing takes them from this row in 990 (an earlier version of this dossier gave them to Cliopatria's Old Kingdom of Norway shape). The Northern Isles were 'Christianised by Olav Tryggvasson in 995'. Jomsborg 'existed between the 960s and 1043' (Jomsborg), so the Wolin cells leave Cliopatria's shape 63 years early.

region.text: the two enclaves of Cliopatria's 793 shape: the Ladoga shore and the Mecklenburg coast

ledger.note: 793: the Viking Age begins. 'The Viking Age in Scandinavian history is taken to have been the period from the earliest recorded raids by Norsemen in 793' (Vikings). Staraya Ladoga (opened): 'A Scandinavian settlement was founded in the mid-8th century' and 'Around the 830s or 840s, it was captured by a group of Varangians', so the Ladoga enclave has a page behind it in substance, though no sentence dates it to 793; nothing opened dates the Mecklenburg coast. The year is the Vikings page's, the core is Cliopatria's.

800: Norse enclave on Shetland. 'Viking influence in the area commenced in the late 8th century'; settlers 'perhaps as early as the mid-7th century' (Norwick, Unst). The year 800 is Cliopatria's; the page gives no year.

800: Norse enclave on the Faroes. Page silent: the Viking expansion article has no dated sentence for the Faroe Islands; year and cells are Cliopatria's. History of the Faroe Islands (opened): 'Norsemen settled the Faroe Islands in the 9th or 10th century' and, per the Flateyjarbok, 'Grimr Kamban settled in Faroe when Harald Harfagre was king of Norway (872-930)', so the page puts settlement later than Cliopatria's 800; still confidence 1 for the year.

825: a five-cell enclave at the Peene mouth appears. Page silent; year and cells are Cliopatria's.
840: Norse enclave on Caithness and Sutherland. 'Caithness and Sutherland fell under Norse control at an early date' (no year given); the year 840 is Cliopatria's.
840: Cliopatria draws the Isle of Man as Norse. The page says Man 'may also have been taken by the Norse in 877' and was 'certainly held by them by 900': the 840 start is probably early (two cells).

ledger.note: 840: a six-cell enclave at the Oder mouth (Wolin) appears. Page silent; year and cells are Cliopatria's. The Vikings page dates Jomsborg 'between the 960s and 1043'.

847: the Norse conquer the Inner Hebrides; Skye and Argyll are Cliopatria's cells beside them, on the land of Dal Riata (Cliopatria row 540-899). 'The Frankish Annales Bertiniani may record the conquest of the Inner Hebrides by Vikings in 847.' The page dates nothing for Skye and says 'Evidence for Norse settlement in mainland Argyll is limited', so the Skye and mainland cells rest on the shape, not the page; the Norse language became dominant in the Inner Hebrides 'during the 10th and 11th centuries'. Cliopatria draws these cells from 840 (keyframe viking-settlements_840 removes them for 840-846); the Dal Riata dossier has the same loss in 847 (ledger 6).

region.text: Friesland and the Rhine-Meuse mouths (Walcheren, Texel)

ledger.note: c. 850: the Danes rule Frisia. Viking expansion (paraphrase): c. 850 Lothair I acknowledged Rorik as ruler of most of Friesland. The year is the page's 'c.'; Lothair I's realm is Cliopatria's Middle Franks (850-899).

840s: Vikings settle at the mouth of the Garonne. Viking expansion (paraphrase): in the 840s Pepin II called in the Vikings against Charles and they settled at the mouth of the Garonne; 850 is the first year of Cliopatria's shape. The counterpart is Charles the Bald's West Francia.
850: a base at Bayonne. The page lists bases at Bayonne, Saint-Florent-le-Vieil and Noirmoutier without a date; the year is Cliopatria's.

850: Cliopatria draws Limerick as Norse. Disagreement: the page (paraphrase) has the Vikings found Waterford, Wexford, Cork and Limerick in the eight years after their return in 914, and says longphorts were built 'From 840'; the 850 cluster is 60+ years earlier than the page's town foundation and rests on Cliopatria alone. Norse-Gaels (opened) names the five towns' kingdoms ('Dublin, Waterford, Wexford, Cork and Limerick') without a year.
850: a seven-cell enclave at Truso on the Vistula lagoon appears. Page silent; year and cells are Cliopatria's.

region.text: Dublin and the coast around it

ledger.note: 853: the Norse kingdom of Dublin. The kingdom 'lasted from roughly 853 AD to 1170 AD'; infobox 'Established: 853'; the Vikings 'may have first over-wintered in 840-841'. Cliopatria's Dublin cells begin in 850. The page gives no counterpart (the Irish kings are not named for 853).
860: Cliopatria draws Waterford as Norse. Disagreement as for Limerick: the page (paraphrase) dates the founding of Waterford, Wexford, Cork and Limerick to the eight years after 914.
860: the Garonne bases drop out of Cliopatria's shape. Page silent on when they ended (the article says only that Vikings 'entered the Garonne' in 844).

862: Rurik is invited to Novgorod. Rurik 'invited to reign in Novgorod in the year 862'; 'In 862, according to Russian sources, Rurik arrived in the eastern Baltic'. Cliopatria draws Novgorod from 860. Primary Chronicle tradition: the tribes had first expelled the Varangians (860-862); Rurik's historicity is disputed.
866: Beloozero. 'Sineus established himself at Beloozero, and Truvor at the town of Izborsk' (Primary Chronicle account, undated on the page); Cliopatria's cluster begins in 866.

866: a 35-cell Danish cluster in Lincolnshire (the Mercian side). Page silent: the Danelaw article dates only the landing in East Anglia (865) and the capture of York (867); the Danelaw 'covered ... the central and eastern Midlands'. Great Heathen Army (opened): the first dated Danish stay in Lincolnshire is 'winter quarters for 872-873 at Torksey in the Kingdom of Lindsey (now part of Lincolnshire)', six years after Cliopatria's cluster; the page has the army take York 'in November 866', one year before the Danelaw page's 867 (867 is kept for the York event).
867: the Danes take York. 'In 867 they captured Northumbria and its capital, York'. Cliopatria adds Yorkshire only in 870 (see keyframe viking-settlements_867).

869: East Anglia falls. 'the Danes continued their invasion in 869 by defeating King Edmund of East Anglia at Hoxne'; the Cliopatria East Anglia row ends 869 and the Viking shape takes the land in 870.
c. 870: Iceland is first settled. 'Iceland was first settled around 870' (Viking expansion); Ingólfr Arnarson 'settled with his family around 874' at Reykjavík; Settlement of Iceland: 'around 874'.

region.text: the Mercian lands the army took in 874-875

ledger.note: 874: Mercia falls to the army. 'the Danes turned to the north and attacked Mercia, a campaign that lasted until 874'. The page does not say what land was taken; the two clusters are Cliopatria's 875 additions.

875: settlement spreads over the west, south and north of Iceland. 'Written sources consider the age of settlement ... to have begun with settlement by Ingólfr Arnarson around 874'; the page gives no regional dates, only that Ingólfr took 'much of the southwest', Flóki the Westfjords, Garðar the north.

region.text: Orkney and Shetland, the Northern Isles

ledger.note: 875: Harald Fairhair takes the Northern Isles. Harald 'incorporated the Northern Isles into his kingdom in 875'.
875: Cliopatria hands Caithness and Sutherland to the Old Kingdom of Norway with the Northern Isles. The page says only that they 'fell under Norse control at an early date'.

875: a Danish foothold on the Dorset coast. Danelaw timeline: '875: The Danes settled in Dorset, well inside Alfred's Kingdom of Wessex, but Alfred quickly made peace with them'; '876: The Danes broke the peace when they captured the fortress of Wareham, followed by a similar capture of Exeter in 877'. The cells are Cliopatria's.

877: a Danish foothold at Exeter. Danelaw timeline: '876: The Danes broke the peace when they captured the fortress of Wareham, followed by a similar capture of Exeter in 877.' The page's body text puts both captures in 876 ('Guthrum and the Danes brokered peace with Wessex in 876, when they captured the fortresses of Wareham and Exeter'); the timeline's 877 is used. Cliopatria draws the three Exeter cells from 876 (keyframe viking-settlements_876 removes them for 876; _877 restores them).
878: the Dorset foothold ends with Guthrum's defeat. 'written following Guthrum's defeat at the Battle of Edington in 878'. Cells leave Cliopatria's shape in 878.
878: the Exeter foothold ends with Guthrum's defeat at Edington (878).

region.text: the Chippenham country in north Wiltshire

ledger.note: 878: Guthrum's army holds the Chippenham country. Page silent on Chippenham; the Edington date (878) is the page's. Three cells, until 880.

region.text: Yorkshire, the East Midlands and East Anglia, the land of the later Danelaw

ledger.note: 878: the Danelaw takes the settled land. 'The Danelaw approximately covered Yorkshire, the central and eastern Midlands, and the East of England'; the treaty 'written following Guthrum's defeat at the Battle of Edington in 878' and formalised 886-890 'defining the boundaries of their kingdoms'. The handover to the Danelaw as a separate row at 878 is Cliopatria's; 26 of the 221 cells lie in Cliopatria's Mercia.
880: the Chippenham cells leave Cliopatria's shape. Page silent.

882: Oleg unites the Varangian north under Kiev. 'his kinsman Oleg captured Kiev in 882 and made it the capital of the Rus' (Vikings); 'Oleg moved the capital to Kiev' (Rurik, undated). The year is the page's; that all four northern enclaves pass to Kievan Rus' in 882 is Cliopatria's (89 of 89 cells).

885: Viking rule of Frisia ends. Viking expansion (paraphrase): Godfrid was assassinated in 885, ending Viking rule of Frisia; he had controlled most of Frisia 882-885. Cliopatria hands the cells to West Franks (and the Carolingian umbrella) in 886. Earlier: Rorik became Charles the Bald's vassal at Nijmegen in 870.

886: a Viking army on the Seine at Paris. Siege of Paris (opened): infobox '25 November 885 - October 886'; 'the Vikings arrived outside Paris in late November 885'; Sigfred 'left the siege in April' while 'Rollo stayed behind with his men'; in October 886 Charles 'allowed the Vikings to sail up the Seine to ravage Burgundy'. The year is the page's siege year and the region is the Seine around Paris; the page has no Oise camp, so the Oise cells are Cliopatria's.

892: the Seine cluster leaves Cliopatria's shape. Page silent for 892: the Siege of Paris page has the Vikings withdraw from France 'the next spring' (887), four years before this year, and does not cover the Seine after that (Montfaucon 888 and Louvain 891 are not on it); the 892 end rests on Cliopatria.

892: a Danish army lands in Kent. Alfred the Great: 'After another lull, in the autumn of 892 or 893, the Danes attacked again'; 'They entrenched themselves, the larger body at Appledore, Kent, and the lesser under Hastein, at Milton, also in Kent.' The seven Kent cells are Cliopatria's; the Wessex dossier has the same landing as a contest (ledger 27).

896: the Danish army gives up. Alfred the Great: 'The next year, 896 (or 897), they gave up the struggle. Some retired to Northumbria, some to East Anglia. Those who had no connections in England returned to the continent.' The page has no later mention of Danes in Kent, so the Kent cells go in 896 although Cliopatria keeps them to 910 (keyframes viking-settlements_897 and _902 remove them). The Wessex dossier's contest ends in 896 as well (ledger 28).

902: the Irish drive the Norse out of Dublin. Ívarr II was 'Driven from Dublin in 902 by native Irish'; 'Dublin abandoned by the Norse from 902 to 917'. Cliopatria keeps Dublin in the shape throughout (see keyframes viking-settlements_902 and 911b).

907: the Norse occupy Brittany. Alan II 'expelled the Vikings/Norsemen from Brittany after an occupation that lasted from 907 to about 939'. The land is the Kingdom of Brittany's (its own page dates the complete occupation from 919, a disagreement left open): it is drawn hatched from this event to 937, not as Viking territory, and the keyframes drop its cells from the Viking shape. Region: the Brittany cells of Cliopatria's 936 shape without the Loire estuary.

907: the Norse occupy Brittany, the Loire estuary included. The page's occupation 'from 907 to about 939' covers the whole country; the estuary is split out because 'By 937 Alan was master of most of Brittany, having forced the Norsemen back to the Loire', so it stays occupied to about 939 (ledger below). Drawn hatched, not as Viking territory.
917: the Norse return to Dublin. 'Dublin abandoned by the Norse from 902 to 917'; Sigtryggr (917-921). The Viking expansion article gives 914 for the return 'led by the Uí Ímair'.

c. 914-922: Cork is founded. Viking expansion (paraphrase): the Vikings returned in 914, 'led by the Uí Ímair', and in 'the next eight years' founded Waterford, Wexford, Cork and Limerick, Ireland's first large towns (the span 914-922 is derived from that phrase).

930: the age of settlement ends and the Althing meets. 'the age of settlement is considered to have ended in the year 930', when the Althing was established; 'fully settled' by 930. Cliopatria's Icelandic Commonwealth row begins 936.

936: Alan II lands at Dol. 'Alan landed at Dol in 936, at the invitation of a monk, Jean de Landévennec, and with the aid of Æthelstan.' The counterpart is the Kingdom of Brittany row (to 939); the Duchy of Brittany dossier starts only in 939.

937: the occupation ends everywhere but the Loire. 'By 937 Alan was master of most of Brittany, having forced the Norsemen back to the Loire.' Last year drawn hatched is 936; the Kingdom of Brittany dossier has the same end (its ledger 8).

939: the last Norse leave the Loire. The occupation 'lasted from 907 to about 939'; Alan built a church 'for his victory in liberating Nantes' (undated). Cliopatria keeps Brittany in the Viking shape until 946; the keyframes drop it. The Kingdom of Brittany dossier has no separate end for the estuary (its 937 event covers all of Brittany).

939: Trans-la-Forêt. 'On 1 August 939, with the aid of Judicael (Berengar), count of Rennes' Alan completed the victory 'by defeating the Norse at the Battle of Trans-la-Forêt'. The page does not name the Loire in connection with the battle; the occupation ended 'about 939'.

region.text: the Mecklenburg coast and the Peene mouth

ledger.note: 947: the Baltic enclaves west of the Oder leave Cliopatria's shape for the Kingdom of Germany row (the Obotrites' own row ends 946). Page silent.

region.text: the Pomeranian coast at the Oder mouth, Jomsborg

ledger.note: 947: a small enclave on the Pomeranian coast. Page silent on 947; the Vikings page says Jomsborg 'existed between the 960s and 1043', which is the probable meaning of the cluster. Jomsborg (opened): 'was built by the Danish king Harold Bluetooth (910-985/86) in the 960s'; 'it is often maintained that Jomsborg was located on the eastern outlet of the Oder river'; 'Jomsborg is often thought to be identical with the present-day town of Wolin'; its location and existence have 'not yet been established'. Cliopatria's 947 start is some 15 years before the page's earliest date.

980: the Wolin cells leave Cliopatria's shape for Poland. Page silent; the Vikings page puts Jomsborg 'between the 960s and 1043'. Jomsborg (opened): 'Jomsborg was destroyed in 1043 by Dano-Norwegian king Magnus the Good', 63 years after the cells leave Cliopatria's shape for Poland; the exit stays on Cliopatria's year.
980: the Limerick cluster leaves Cliopatria's shape. Page silent on Limerick; the article says only that Máel Sechnaill Mór defeated the Dublin Vikings at the Battle of Tara in 980.

region.text: the last Baltic enclaves (Truso and the Oder mouth)

ledger.note: 1000: the last Baltic cells leave Cliopatria's shape (6 of 15 fall inside Cliopatria's Poland). Page silent; Jomsborg 'existed between the 960s and 1043'. Jomsborg (opened) has it 'destroyed in 1043'; the exit stays on Cliopatria's year.

1021: the Norse at L'Anse aux Meadows. 'Trees at L'Anse aux Meadows were felled by the Norse in 1021' (tree rings); the site 'may have been used as late as 1145 AD'. Cliopatria has it only in 1000-1017.

1022: the camp is given up. Page silent on the end; the Vikings page calls it 'a short-lived settlement'; the Norse colonization page says the site 'may have been used as late as 1145 AD'. One year is drawn (bridging judgment). L'Anse aux Meadows (opened): the site was 'occupied at least sporadically for perhaps 20 years' (Steinberg), 'the inhabitants abandoned the site in an orderly fashion' (Barraclough), radiocarbon 'between 990 and 1050 CE'; the page gives no abandonment year.

1035: the Faroes pass to the Old Kingdom of Norway. History of the Faroe Islands: 'The Faroes became a part of the Kingdom of Norway in 1035.' The page also has Sigmundur Brestisson sent 'to take possession of the islands for Olaf Tryggvason, king of Norway' and 'Norwegian supremacy was upheld and continued', so Norwegian claims are older than the page's date; 1035 is the page's. The four cells are Cliopatria's; the Norway dossier has the same gain (its ledger 14).

1079: Godred Crovan takes Mann and founds the Crovan dynasty. Scandinavian Scotland: 'Godred Crovan became the ruler of Dublin and Mann from 1079'; 'The Isle of Man may also have been taken by the Norse in 877 and was certainly held by them by 900.' Until 1079 the two Man cells stay in this row; no page opened puts them under Norway before 1098 (the Norway dossier's vassal event). The Isles dossier founds its kingdom on Man in 1079 (its ledger 0, with no counterpart named).

1085: the Hebrides pass to Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Isles. Scandinavian Scotland: the Hebrides and the islands of the Clyde 'were essentially under the control of rulers of Scandinavian origin from "at least the late tenth century"'; 'Magnus Barelegs re-established direct Norwegian overlordship there by 1098'; the Crovan dynasty 'ruled as "Kings of Mann and the Isles"' from the early 12th century. The page dates no handover in 1085: the year is the Isles dossier's (its ledger 1, which takes these cells from this row at confidence 1) and Cliopatria's Isles shape. From 990 to 1085 no page puts these islands under a state, so this row keeps them.

1171: the Normans take Dublin. 'The last king of Dublin was killed by the Norman conquerors of Dublin in 1171' (the infobox says 'Norman conquest: 1170'). The conquerors are the Anglo-Normans under the Angevin Henry II; Cliopatria's Angevin Empire row covers the Dublin cells from 1177.

1171: the last Norse enclave falls and the row ends. After Dublin, the shape keeps Waterford, Wexford, Cork and Limerick, which Cliopatria's Angevin Empire (1177) and Kingdom of England (1210) rows cover; every other cell has already left this row (the Faroes to Norway in 1035, Man in 1079 and the Hebrides in 1085 to the Kingdom of the Isles; Greenland is the Norse Greenland dossier's). The page dates only Dublin; the Irish towns' fall is on no page opened (Norse-Gaels, opened: 'These kingdoms did not survive the subsequent Norman invasions', undated).

wars.name: Great Heathen Army

zones.text: Northumbria (York, 867), East Anglia (Hoxne, 869) and Mercia (to 874): the land of the later Danelaw

wars.outcome: The Danes land in East Anglia in 865, take York (867), defeat East Anglia (869) and Mercia (874); Alfred defeats Guthrum at Edington in 878 and the Treaty of Alfred and Guthrum (886-890) fixes the Danelaw's boundary.
wars.note: The Viking expansion page adds: 871 the army is reinforced by the Great Summer Army under Guthrum; 875 it splits; 876 Halfdan shares out Northumbria.

wars.name: Godfrid's invasion of Frisia

zones.text: Frisia, 'most of Frisia' held by Godfrid 882-885

wars.outcome: Godfrid arrives in Frisia c. 879 with a large force, controls most of it 882-885 (siege of Asselt, 882) and is assassinated in 885, ending Viking rule of Frisia.
wars.note: Rorik, Godfrid's predecessor, was acknowledged by Lothair I c. 850 and became Charles the Bald's vassal at Nijmegen in 870.

wars.name: Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte

zones.text: Rouen and the lower Seine: Rollo's grant

wars.outcome: Rollo enters vassalage to Charles the Simple and becomes the first Norman count of Rouen; the Duchy of Normandy dossier carries the land from 911 (Cliopatria's 911-921 Viking shape is corrected to leave it out).

wars.name: Expulsion of the Norse from Dublin
wars.outcome: Ívarr II is driven from Dublin by the native Irish in 902; the Norse hold nothing there until Sigtryggr returns in 917 (914 in the Viking expansion article).

wars.name: Battle of Clontarf
belligerents: Irish kings (Máel Sechnaill Mór, Brian Boru)
wars.outcome: Máel Sechnaill Mór defeats the Dublin Vikings at Tara (980); Gaelic conquest of Dublin led by Máel Sechnaill in 988 (Kingdom of Dublin); Glenmama (999); Clontarf (1014) ended the Dublin Vikings' ability to threaten Ireland's most powerful kings. Dublin stays a Norse kingdom until 1171.
wars.note: No territorial result: Dublin remained Norse; the entry lists the sequence so the reviewer can see it was considered.

wars.name: Reconquest of Brittany by Alan II
wars.outcome: Alan II lands at Dol in 936 with Æthelstan's aid, is master of most of Brittany by 937 with the Norsemen forced back to the Loire, and ends the occupation of 907 to about 939 at Trans-la-Forêt on 1 August 939. The Kingdom of Brittany is the occupied state; the Duchy of Brittany starts in 939.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Dublin
wars.outcome: The last king of Dublin is killed by the Norman conquerors in 1171 (the infobox says the Norman conquest was 1170).
wars.note: The page calls the conquerors 'Norman'; the counterpart slug angevin-empire is the reading of Henry II's lordship and Cliopatria's row that covers Dublin from 1177.

certainty.note: Raiding bases and first settlements with no fixed frontier: every enclave is Cliopatria's approximate cluster of cells.
Scattered enclaves with no surveyed frontier. The only fixed line is the Danelaw boundary of the 886-890 treaty, which belongs to the Danelaw row, not to this state.

notes:
What this dossier is. 'Viking settlements' is not one state: Cliopatria draws a scatter of Norse-held enclaves (Ladoga, Rostov, Frisia, Dublin, the Danelaw before 878, Normandy, Brittany, Iceland, Greenland, the Hebrides and more) as one polity with 28 shapes (793..1332, 5,754 to 134,483 km2), and the colour agent needs a slug for them. It is typed 'state' so that it is drawn; each enclave had its own rulers (Rorik, Rollo, the kings of Dublin, Ingolfr, Erik the Red) and no capital, so capitals and rulers are empty. The Vikings article has no infobox area, so no area comparison could be made.

Choices that depart from Cliopatria, and why (reviewers and gap-fillers read this first; repaired 2026-10-25 after review).
1. The dossier ends in 1171, not 1332. The Kingdom of Dublin page dates the last Norse king's death to 1171 (infobox: Norman conquest 1170). From 1035 on, most cells of the row are also in another Cliopatria row or another dossier: the Faroes (4 cells) in the Old Kingdom of Norway's shape from 1040 (the Faroes page puts them in Norway in 1035), Greenland (the identical 78 cells) in Norse Greenland, the Irish towns in the Angevin Empire (1177) and England (1210) rows. Those overlaps were computed with the gazetteer. The corrected keyframes (viking-settlements_1000, _1003, _1018, _1028, _1035, _1079, _1085) remove the duplicated cells; if the eu-14 and eu-11 dossiers narrow those rows, restore the cells from Cliopatria's shapes. The 1326-1332 shape (two cells) is marked wrong.
2. The Hebrides, Skye, Argyll and Man (27 cells) stay in this row until they go to the Kingdom of the Isles: Man in 1079 (Godred Crovan), the Hebrides in 1085 (the Isles dossier's year). No page opened puts them under Norway before 1098: Scandinavian Scotland has the Hebrides under Scandinavian rulers from 'at least the late tenth century' and 'direct Norwegian overlordship' re-established 'by 1098'. An earlier version gave them to Cliopatria's Old Kingdom of Norway shape in 990 on a computed overlap, which left the land with no owner for about 90 years; the Norway dossier cuts the same isles from its 990 shape. Cliopatria's own 1000-1017 Viking shapes omit them, and the corrections add them back from the 1028 shape.
3. Brittany. Alan II's page dates the Norse occupation of Brittany 'from 907 to about 939'. It is an occupation of the Kingdom of Brittany, not Viking territory: the ledger carries it as occupation events (907 to 937, the Loire estuary to about 939) and a contest from Alan's landing at Dol (936) to Trans-la-Foret (1 August 939), all with kingdom-of-brittany as counterpart, and the keyframes take Brittany and the Cotentin (139 cells) out of Cliopatria's Viking shape for 922-946. The Kingdom of Brittany dossier dates the complete occupation from 919 (919 there, 907 here: a flagged disagreement). The Cotentin goes to Normandy in 933 (Duchy of Normandy and Kingdom of Brittany dossiers); Duchy of Brittany starts only in 939.
4. Normandy. Rollo 'entered vassalage to Charles the Simple' in 911 and became the first Norman count of Rouen (Viking expansion). A West Frankish vassal county is not Viking territory, and the Duchy of Normandy dossier founds the duchy in 911 on the same land, so the 36 Normandy cells are removed from the 911-921 shapes. An earlier version held them here to 921.
5. Iceland leaves in 930 (the Althing, end of the age of settlement), the year the Icelandic Commonwealth dossier starts, although Cliopatria's Icelandic Commonwealth row begins 936.
6. Greenland is not this row's. The Norse Greenland dossier founds the colony in 986 on the Greenland settlements (its ledger 0, keyframe _986: 'Norse settlements in Greenland were established after 986 CE', Norse Greenland); Cliopatria's Viking row also draws the same cells for 1000-1071 and Norse Greenland from 1072. The cells are removed from every corrected shape here to avoid a double claim for 986-1071, and the earlier gain (986) and loss (1072) events are gone. No page dates 1072.
7. L'Anse aux Meadows is dated 1021 by the Norse colonization page (tree rings); Cliopatria has it 1000-1017. The page does not date the camp's end ('occupied at least sporadically for perhaps 20 years', L'Anse aux Meadows); the one-year keyframe 1021 and the 1022 loss are a bridging judgment (confidence 1).
8. York (867) and East Anglia (869) are dated by the Danelaw page; Cliopatria adds them in 870. The Inner Hebrides fall in 847 (Scandinavian Scotland, Annales Bertiniani 'may record'), seven years after Cliopatria's 840; Exeter is 877 on the Danelaw timeline (876 in its body text), Cliopatria's 876; the Danes leave Kent in 896 (Alfred the Great), Cliopatria's 911; the Faroes join Norway in 1035 (History of the Faroe Islands), Cliopatria's 1040.

Not settled (page silent within the budget). Rostov, Beloozero and the Baltic enclaves (Mecklenburg, Rugen, Peene, Oder mouth, Truso) have no dated sentence in any page opened (Staraya Ladoga: Scandinavian settlement from the mid-8th century, no Rostov or Beloozero); they are confidence 1 or flagged 'unverified: page budget'. The eight Mecklenburg cells last exactly as long as the Obotrites row (793-946) and may be Obotrite land. The Oder-mouth cluster may be Jomsborg ('between the 960s and 1043', Jomsborg), which the shape starts 15 years early and ends 63 years early. The 35-cell Lincolnshire cluster of 866 (the Great Heathen Army page has the first Lindsey winter quarters in 872-873), the Seine cluster 886-891 (the Siege of Paris page ends at the spring of 887), Chippenham 878-879, Man from 840 (Scandinavian Scotland: 'may also have been taken by the Norse in 877', 'certainly held by them by 900') and the four cells inside Norway (1003, 1028+) rest on Cliopatria alone. Limerick (850) and Waterford (860) conflict with the Viking expansion page, which has the towns founded in the eight years after 914 (the Norse-Gaels page names them without dates). The Dublin return is 914 on the Viking expansion page and 917 on the Kingdom of Dublin page (917 used); the Norman conquest is 1170 in the infobox and 1171 in the body (1171 used). The Great Heathen Army page has York taken in November 866, the Danelaw page 867 (867 used). The Kent occupation is typed occupation here and contest in the Wessex dossier (ledger 27-28), both 892-896. Rurik's 862 is the Primary Chronicle's date and the page treats him as semi-legendary.

Needs other dossiers or other pages. Rorik became Charles the Bald's vassal in 870 (Viking expansion): the west-franks dossier may carry a vassal event for Frisia that names this state as counterpart. Eric Bloodaxe took York in 947 and was driven out in 954 (Danelaw, Viking expansion): that is the danelaw and kingdom-of-northumbria dossiers' ledger, not this one. The Kingdom of the Isles dossier founds its kingdom on Man in 1079 without naming this state as counterpart (its ledger 0) and gives Dublin to the Isles in 1094-1095 (its ledger 2-3) while this row keeps Dublin to 1171. The rus dossier founds Oleg's Rus' in 880 on the northern enclaves that this row holds to 881 (loss in 882, the Vikings page), a two-year overlap. The kingdom-of-dublin dossier (853 to 1170) and kingdom-of-leinster, which exist now, also claim Dublin from 853, the land this row holds too (except 902-917): one of the two should keep it. The Irish towns' fall (Waterford, Wexford, Cork, Limerick, 1170s) wants a page of Hiberno-Norse towns; the Angevin dossier has no event naming this state.

Gazetteer names used and checked (all resolve): places Staraya Ladoga, Rostock, Yaroslavl, Kirkwall, Elblag, Veliky Novgorod, Dublin, Limerick, York, Cambridge, Cork, Nantes; admin1 Shetland Islands and Eilean Siar (United Kingdom); country Isle of Man, Iceland. Not in the gazetteer: Orkney, Shetland, Caithness, Skye, Argyll, Faroe Islands, Greenland's two settlements, Danelaw, Beloozero, Wolin, Bayonne; they are written as radii around coordinates intersected with the Cliopatria shape of the year.
